1.explanation: The Elixir language definition in components/prism-elixir.js (and its minified counterpart) defines the “attr-name” token using a regex that matches only word characters followed by a colon. It does not allow an optional trailing question mark, so keys like attribute? are not seen as attr-name tokens. Updating the regex in these files to include an optional ‘?’ before the colon fixes the highlighting for predicate-style attribute names.
1.bug_scenario: On the PrismJS test page, Elixir map attributes ending with a question mark (e.g. attribute?) are not being tokenized as attr-name. In the screenshot the key attribute: is highlighted correctly, but attribute?: is not recognized as an attr-name token and therefore not styled.

2.explanation: Both of these files define the Elixir language syntax rules, including the “attr-name” token pattern around line 40. The existing regex, which matches word characters followed by a colon, does not include an optional question mark before the colon, so attribute names ending with “?” are never tokenized correctly. Updating the regex in these files to allow a trailing “?” (for example, changing `/\w+?:(?!:)/` to `/\w+?\?:(?!:)/`) will ensure that attribute? is properly recognized and highlighted.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Elixir code, attribute names that end with a question mark (e.g. attribute?) are not recognized as tokens. In the Prism “Test drive” screenshot, you can see that “attribute:” is correctly highlighted as an attr-name token, but “attribute?:” is not highlighted at all. This is because the regex for the “attr-name” token in the Elixir grammar doesn’t allow a trailing “?”.
